evidence.note: Agent starts server node 0, gets a health response, then a curl|python3 pipe hangs. This is the divergence point — the server stops responding — but instead of revising the server design, the agent enters a recovery loop.

~80 steps of the same recovery tactics repeated verbatim (Ctrl+C, killall, tmux respawn-pane, new-window). Same fix applied in circles with no strategic re-think despite continuous failure — the anchor-0 pattern.

The single moment of real root-cause reasoning: hypothesizes gevent monkey-patching was omitted so Redis pubsub listen() blocks the event loop, and plans to add monkey-patching. Genuine diagnosis of a broken invariant — but it is never applied or re-verified because control is never regained.

After the step-108 insight, the agent reverts to the identical circular kill/tmux attempts for another ~70 steps and the trajectory ends still stuck, never acting on its own diagnosis and never testing seq/fan-out/resilience invariants at all.

reasoning: The agent never reached the distributed invariants this dimension targets; the divergence it actually faced (a hung server) was met with ~150 steps of the same recovery commands repeated in circles, never abandoning a failing strategy — the anchor-0 behavior. A single unapplied, unverified root-cause hypothesis at step 108 (gevent/Redis blocking) lifts it just above pure 0, so I score 1.
